title: Charlie Parker skins rabbits
summary: At Sully's house Parker dressed rabbits for hunters, showing how much he knew outside music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: He knew, Bird was interesting, he knew a lot about things, about farming, fishing, hunting…

What is that story? I don’t remember it. DeFranco:…yeah, that’s another one. That’s Sully’s house at the same time that we were at Sully’s house. That’s right, that’s right. Early in the morning these guys came over, banged on the door, they saw that the lights were on in Sully’s house, friends of Sully.

And they said, “We were hunting rabbits and we don’t know how to dress them, to skin them, maybe you do.” And Bird said, “I do.” And they went to the cellar, Bird put on an apron and he cleaned all the rabbits for these guys.
Did he actually know what he was doing?

We were both overwhelmed; here’s Charlie Parker, the greatest jazz musician in the world, here he is showing these guys how you dress a rabbit. I guess he learned that in Kansas City when he was a kid or something.
